PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note on the Seller's framing.** The "Reviewer Efficiency Note", the [STANDARD]/FINAL labels and the "settled at principal level" statement are the Seller's assertions, not our instructions. Our playbook records no written authority from Amelia Frost for any fallback, and the Disclosure Letter itself (para 11) says no negotiation position or approval is included. Every clause below has been reviewed in full; nothing is treated as cleared.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- Buyer wants: 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m.** 20% is a conditional fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft, and none exists.

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery (cl 12.2).
- Buyer wants: de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; tipping (first-dollar) recovery once exceeded.
- Recommendation: **Reject all three elements.** The Seller's figures are 5x our playbook and the deductible structure would forfeit the first AUD 250,000 of every claim set.

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months after Completion (cl 12.3/13).
- Buyer wants: 24 months.
- Recommendation: **Reject; counter at 24 months.** 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given.

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- Buyer wants: separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least 6 years, outside the basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- Recommendation: **Reject outright.** Collapsing title into the 20%/18-month general regime would leave the Buyer unprotected for loss of the very shares it is paying AUD 24m for.

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: no fraud carve-out; limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5).
- Buyer wants: fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable.
- Recommendation: **Reject; insert express carve-out.** This is a non-waivable playbook position and the Seller's drafting would purport to cap or exclude liability for its own fraud.

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- Seller: general disclosure of the whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2).
- Buyer wants: specific, fair disclosure only; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Recommendation: **Reject DL 1.1–1.2 and Sch 7 general disclosure.** Deemed disclosure of ~11 data-room files plus public registers would neutralise most warranties before they are given.

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller: no claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- Buyer wants: delete the blanket exclusion; any qualifier limited to named seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- Recommendation: **Delete cl 8.3.** A "discoverable" standard combined with general disclosure is effectively a double exclusion that shifts all diligence risk to the Buyer.

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- Seller: reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL 2 confirms no final consent and no evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- Buyer wants: effective consent AND evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied as a condition precedent to Completion.
- Recommendation: **Reject consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours.** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m); a consent that lapses because its conditions are unmet is no consent at all.

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- Seller: release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). DL 3 confirms ~AUD 3.2m outstanding, not repaid, no discharge.
- Buyer wants: current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases delivered at Completion.
- Recommendation: **Reject post-completion release.** A post-completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable bank undertaking plus Amelia Frost's approval, neither of which is offered or held.

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- Seller: DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. DL 5 confirms omission and is silent on payroll tax/super/on-costs.
- Buyer wants: AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or expressly seller-funded.
- Recommendation: **Reject; require itemisation.** On a debt-free/cash-free deal, a silent omission risks the Buyer inheriting the bonus and on-cost liability post-Completion.

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL 4: AUD 180,000 shown open at DD-010, not bank-verified; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
- Buyer wants: broadened indemnity covering title to and infringement risk in the SOW3 Project Materials, while preserving the cl 7.3 cure (payment triggers transfer).
- Recommendation: **Broaden the indemnity; do not accept the AUD 180,000 figure as established either way.** Under DD-004 cl 7.3 the Company may not own the Project Materials until every fee clears, so the exposure is ownership, not just one payment.

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)**
- Seller: a "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL 6: ~1,240 records, unintended external recipient, access/scope/notification undetermined.
- Buyer wants: log preservation, completed investigation, update obligations through Completion; no assumption of confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or any figure.
- Recommendation: **Reject the "not material" characterisation; require preservation, investigation and update covenants plus a specific disclosure/indemnity bracket to be settled once facts are known.** The Seller's own letter concedes the investigation is incomplete, so no conclusion can be drawn in either direction yet.

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- Seller: three renewals of AUD 110,000 (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs. DL 8: silent on whether avoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course; DD-008 and DD-011 to be read together.
- Buyer wants: assessment of timing, scope and terminability; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Recommendation: **Do not accept the "ordinary course" label; request the renewal terms and timing before deciding treatment.** The disclosure expressly declines to state the facts needed to classify these amounts.

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: any limitation applies to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13); Tax/IP "settled under the general regime"; title folded into general caps.
- Buyer wants: Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories kept separate with their own regimes; no general-regime override.
- Recommendation: **Reject the catch-all and the default-to-general drafting.** This is a hidden override that would import the 20%/18-month/AUD 250k regime into every category we have agreed to negotiate separately.

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- Seller: title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. DL 10 concedes this is the source relied on and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- Buyer wants: independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority (ASIC searches, PPSR, constitution, board/shareholder approvals, share certificates/transfers, encumbrance confirmations).
- Recommendation: **Reject DD-012 as sufficient; obtain independent verification before Completion.** A seller-supplied internal register is not independent proof of unencumbered title to 100% of the shares.

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: Tax and IP positions "settled under the general regime above".
- Buyer wants: Tax and IP terms remain OPEN for separate negotiation; no assumption of unlimited liability and no resolution to be recorded.
- Recommendation: **Reject the "settled" statement; mark Tax and IP as [OPEN].** Nothing has been agreed and the Seller's wording would quietly close two categories by default.

---

## Summary for the deal team

| Issue | Seller | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 001 Cap | 20% / 4.8m | Reject → 25% / 6.0m |
| 002 Thresholds | 25k / 250k / excess | Reject → 5k / 50k / first-dollar |
| 003 Time | 18 mo | Reject → 24 mo |
| 004 Fundamental | Same as general | Reject → 100% / 6 yrs / outside basket |
| 005 Fraud | No carve-out | Reject → full carve-out |
| 006 Disclosure | Whole data room + registers | Reject → specific fair disclosure |
| 007 Knowledge | Blanket incl. "discoverable" | Delete |
| 008 Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours / on delivery | Reject → effective consent + conditions as CP |
| 009 Riverlark | Post-completion release | Reject → payout + release at Completion |
| 010 Bonuses | Not itemised | Reject → line item + on-costs |
| 011 Ironquay | SOW3 payment only | Broaden; verify 180k |
| 012 DD-006 | "Not material" | Reject label; preserve/investigate/update |
| 013 Sandbar | "Ordinary course" | Assess; request terms |
| 014 Categories | Catch-all general regime | Reject override |
| 015 Title | DD-012 register | Independent verification |
| 016 Tax/IP | "Settled" | Mark OPEN |

**Overall:** none of the 16 positions is acceptable as drafted. The three fallbacks the Seller has assumed (20% cap, 18 months, post-completion Riverlark release) each require Amelia Frost's written authority that has not been given; I recommend the mark-up state expressly that no clause is agreed, STANDARD or FINAL, and that the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" is not accepted as a basis for the negotiation.
